newsitem.title: CHINA: Canada's Axworthy urges HK to hold open elections.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Axworthy urges HK to hold open elections.

text.p: Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy urged Hong Kong on Wednesday to ensure parliamentary elections due within a year are as open as possible.
Axworthy said on the second day of Beijing's Hong Kong rule that Canada wanted the new legislative polls to be representative of all interest groups.

Beijing retook the former British colony from London at midnight on Monday, and replaced Hong Kong's elected legislature with an appointed chamber until a new assembly is formed through an election next May.
Some pro-democracy campaigners fear a new poll system will favour pro-China candidates.

Axworthy told reporters after meeting the territory's new post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa: "We just made the case that it would be very important for the international community, Canada included, to see an election that would be as open as possible,"
He also said he had also discussed with Tung post-handover issues such as the provision of judges at the Court of Final Appeal and the implementation of U.N. covenants. He did not elaborate.
The Sino-British Joint Declaration, a 1984 pledge governing Hong Kong's sovereignty transfer, was lodged with the U.N. in 1985.
